subject: ss-general-medicine
title: Lysosomal storage and inborn errors in adults

steps.tx: **Lysosomal storage disorders** (genetic failures to digest waste inside the cell lysosome) present in adults far more often than textbooks suggest. **Glucocerebrosidase deficiency** (missing enzyme in type 1 Gaucher disease) fills liver spleen and marrow with lipid laden cells. **Hepatosplenomegaly** (enlarged liver and spleen) with **bone pain** (deep aching from marrow packing) and **cytopenias** (low blood counts) form the adult triad that prompts enzyme testing.
steps.say: Lysosomal storage disorders arise when waste cannot be digested inside the cell, and adults present with them more often than students expect. The commonest adult type can fill liver, spleen and marrow with lipid laden cells. Enlarged organs, deep bone pain, and low blood counts form the triad that should trigger enzyme testing. Splenomegaly with bone crisis is the bedside pattern worth memorising.

steps.tx: **Gaucher disease** (glucocerebrosidase deficiency type 1) spares the brain and follows a chronic course. **Erlenmeyer flask deformity** (a bone end that balloons outward) on knee imaging marks long standing marrow disease. **Idiopathic thrombocytopenia** that resists steroids in an adult with a huge spleen should reopen the diagnosis. **Bone marrow biopsy** (microscopy of marrow tissue) shows wrinkled cells that clinch the morphology although enzyme assay confirms it.
steps.say: Gaucher disease type one can spare the brain and run a chronic course through adult life. Ballooned bone ends on knee imaging, called Erlenmeyer flask deformity, mark long standing marrow packing. Low platelets that resist steroids in a patient with huge splenomegaly should reopen the diagnosis. Marrow microscopy shows wrinkled cells, but enzyme assay confirms the defect.

steps.tx: **Fabry disease** (alpha galactosidase A deficiency) declares itself through skin, eyes, kidneys and nerves together. **Angiokeratomas** (small red skin spots over groin and umbilicus) and **cornea verticillata** (a whorled corneal haze) sit beside **acroparaesthesias** (burning pain in hands and feet). **Nephropathy** (protein losing kidney disease) with **left ventricular hypertrophy** (thickened heart muscle) completes a pattern that single organ clinics often split apart.
steps.say: Fabry disease can link skin, eyes, kidneys, nerves and heart through one enzyme failure. Small red skin spots called angiokeratomas and a whorled corneal haze sit beside burning hand and foot pain. Protein losing kidney disease and thickened heart muscle complete the picture. Clinicians who split these clues between separate clinics often miss the unifying diagnosis for years.

steps.tx: **Pompe disease** (acid maltase deficiency) strikes adult muscle more than childhood models suggest. **Proximal muscle weakness** (hip and shoulder girdle failure) with **girdle pain** (aching around the pelvis) mimics inflammatory myopathy. **Respiratory failure** (falling lung capacity at night) and **macroglossia** (a large tongue) orient late onset cases. **Creatine kinase** (a muscle enzyme in blood) stays modestly raised rather than climbing to myositis heights.
steps.say: Pompe disease attacks muscle through acid maltase failure and reaches adult attention later than childhood models suggest. Hip and shoulder weakness can mimic inflammatory myopathy but without the high muscle enzyme levels. Nighttime breathing failure and a large tongue orient the late onset form. That modest enzyme pattern plus respiratory dominance should push the clinician toward dried blood enzyme testing.

steps.tx: **Niemann Pick disease type C** (a cholesterol trafficking defect) balances nerve and liver signs. **Splenomegaly** (a palpable spleen) with **vertical gaze palsy** (failure to look up and down) and **late cerebellar ataxia** (unsteady walking from brain coordination loss) occur together. **Neonatal jaundice** (yellow skin at birth) in the newborn history and **psychosis** (severe mental disturbance) in adolescence complete a story often filed under unrelated headings.
steps.say: Niemann Pick disease type C can block cholesterol movement inside the cell and mix liver with nerve signs. A palpable spleen, failure to look upward, and unsteady walking from brain coordination loss occur together. Newborn jaundice in the history and psychosis in adolescence can complete a story that often gets filed under separate headings. That combination should trigger filipin staining and gene testing.

steps.tx: **Mucopolysaccharidoses** (sugar chain digestion failures) produce adult joint and corneal disease. **Urinary glycosaminoglycans** (sugar fragments excreted in urine) rise in these disorders and serve as the first screen. **Corneal clouding** (hazy clear windows of the eye) with **stiff joints** (contracted fingers) and **coarse facies** (thickened facial features) point clinicians toward the correct enzyme assay. **MPS type 2** (Hunter disease) spares the cornea and follows X linked passage.
steps.say: Mucopolysaccharidoses block digestion of sugar chains and produce joint stiffness with corneal clouding in adults. Sugar fragments in urine serve as the first screening test. Stiff contracted fingers and thickened facial features point toward enzyme assay, which then names the subtype. One type spares the cornea and follows X linked passage, a detail examiners love to test.

steps.tx: **Adult metabolic presentations** (episodic crashes in grown patients) include hidden urea cycle and fatty acid defects. **Hyperammonaemia** (raised ammonia causing confusion) without liver failure in a woman after childbirth points toward ornithine transcarbamylase carrier disease. **Rhabdomyolysis** (muscle breakdown with dark urine) during fasting or illness suggests fatty acid oxidation failure. **Plasma amino acids** (blood building blocks) and **urine organic acids** (acid fragments in urine) together map the block.
steps.say: Adult metabolic crashes are easily mistaken for psychiatric or infective episodes. Confusion with raised ammonia but no liver failure after childbirth points toward a urea cycle carrier state. Muscle breakdown with dark urine during fasting suggests fat burning failure. Blood amino acids and urine organic acids together can map the metabolic block. Keeping these diagnoses alive in confused young adults saves lives.

steps.tx: **Enzyme replacement therapy** (infused working enzyme taken up by cells) changed Gaucher and Fabry outcomes. **Imiglucerase** (recombinant glucocerebrosidase for Gaucher disease) shrinks spleen and restores blood counts. **Agalsidase** (recombinant alpha galactosidase for Fabry disease) slows kidney decline when started before scarring. **Substrate reduction therapy** (drugs that lower waste production) offers an oral route for milder Gaucher disease in adults unable to receive infusions.
steps.say: Enzyme replacement therapy infuses working enzyme that cells take up and use. Imiglucerase can shrink the spleen in Gaucher disease and restore blood counts over months. Agalsidase slows kidney decline in Fabry disease when started before scarring becomes fixed. Substrate reduction tablets lower waste production and suit selected adults with milder Gaucher disease who cannot manage infusions.

steps.tx: **Haematopoietic stem cell transplantation** (replacement of marrow with donor cells) remains curative for some storage disorders. **Enzyme producing marrow** (donor cells that secrete working enzyme) cross corrects neighbouring tissues without direct delivery. **Conditioning toxicity** (damage from pre transplant chemotherapy) limits this option in fragile adults. **Newborn screening** (early diagnosis from heel prick samples) now speeds referral before organ damage becomes irreversible.
steps.say: Stem cell transplantation can cure some storage disorders by replacing marrow with donor cells that produce working enzyme. Those cells cross correct neighbouring tissues without any direct delivery. Toxicity from pre transplant chemotherapy can limit this option in fragile adults. Newborn screening from heel prick samples now speeds referral before organ damage becomes irreversible in many regions.

steps.tx: **Prognosis** (expected outcome with treatment) depends on early recognition more than drug novelty. **Enzyme therapy** (lifelong replacement infusions) controls visceral disease yet spares brain and bone partly, so **neutralising antibodies** (host defence against the infused protein) can blunt benefit over years. **Family screening** (testing siblings once one case is found) finds milder adults who benefit swiftly. **Genetic counselling** (explaining recurrence before pregnancy) closes the loop for each family.
steps.say: Prognosis can depend on early recognition more than on the novelty of any single drug. Enzyme therapy controls visceral disease well yet reaches brain and bone only partly, and host antibodies against the infused protein can blunt benefit over years. Testing siblings once one case is found uncovers milder adults who benefit swiftly. Counselling about recurrence before pregnancy closes the loop for each family.

steps.tx: **High yield for the exam** links enzyme, sign, and test in one breath. **Gaucher** means glucocerebrosidase loss with huge spleen and Erlenmeyer flask bone, **Fabry** means alpha galactosidase loss with angiokeratomas and cornea verticillata, **Pompe** means acid maltase loss with proximal weakness and respiratory failure, **mucopolysaccharidoses** mean urinary sugar fragments, and **Niemann Pick C** means gaze palsy with splenomegaly. **Dried blood enzyme assay** confirms most adult cases.
steps.say: High yield for the exam can link enzyme, sign, and test in one breath. Gaucher is glucocerebrosidase loss with huge spleen and Erlenmeyer flask bone, Fabry is alpha galactosidase loss with angiokeratomas and cornea verticillata, Pompe is acid maltase loss with proximal weakness and respiratory failure, mucopolysaccharidoses can show sugar fragments in urine, and Niemann Pick type C can show gaze palsy with splenomegaly. Dried blood enzyme assay can confirm most adult cases.
